title: 100x percentage mis-scaling in R3 report and claims ledger (published 0.0185% for 4/216 = 1.85%)
root_cause: Treated the unit fraction 0.0185 (= 4/216) as if it were a percentage, and inverted the unit-lint rule text so it claimed the correct 1.85% figure was the mis-scaling.
what_went_wrong: Report R3 sections 1/2/3/5/10/13 published '0.0185%' - 100x too small; correct value is 4/216 = 1.85%.
e1_claims_ledger unit-lint rule was inverted: it rejected the correct figure and endorsed the wrong one.
r2_2_corrected.md:17 and p1_rootcause.md:118 carried the wrong 0.0185% figure.
detection: External-review follow-up audit of report claims vs evidence arithmetic.

correction.figures: All claim figures corrected to n/N = x% form: 4/216 = 1.85% (or 0.0185 as explicit unit fraction).
correction.lint_rule: Rewritten to require both denominator and computed percentage; bare fractions/percentages and mismatched scalings are rejected.
correction.verification: grep -rn '0.0185' /opt/dr-benchmark/p-chain/ returns only historical raw logs (p1.log unit-fraction 'rate 0.0185', log timestamp false positive) and intentional correction prose; no remaining wrong claim figures. r2_2_corrected.txt verified raw-TSV evidence, no prose to fix.
